header.name: Moral Philosophy and Literature
header.description: This course explores the intersection of literature and moral philosophy. It seeks to expose students to key conceptual relationships between moral philosophy and literature through reading of key philosophical texts. Philosophical texts will be read side by side and complemented with literary texts to understand the conception of morality that underpin literature. The course will ask whether some moral concepts and moral understanding can be developed better through philosophy/literature. What conception of morality can be discerned through reading of literary texts? The central question of this course is whether literature can evoke from us the fineness of perception requisite for moral judgement. This analysis will be done through exposure to philosophical works that do not merely visualise literature as an instance of moral inquiry rather see it as a site of moral inquiry. In doing so it will explore key role that literature can play in expanding moral judgement, imagination, vision, and attention towards doing what is right. The course begins with a brief discussion of the strengths and limitations of the mainstream approaches in ethics. It then explores literature's role in enabling moral reflection by engaging with prominent philosophical works at the intersection of philosophy and literature. Broad topics to be covered include : Literature and Moral judgement, Literature and Moral Imagination, Literature and Moral Vision, Literature and Attention, Literature and Acknowledgement, Thinking through dilemmas in Epics. Specific topics for instruction will be conveyed by the instructor at the beginning of the semester.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop keen understanding of intersections between morality and literature

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to explain, evaluate, and defend philosophical positions
